lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Job Readiness: Applications, Resumes, and Interviews
lessonRef.title: Launch and planning: building a resume from real experience

objective: Learners inventory their real experience (school activities, volunteering, informal work, projects, and extracurriculars) and translate at least four items into resume-ready bullet points using an action verb and a concrete result, without inventing anything that did not happen.
scenario: The learner lists every real activity that could belong on a first resume, then rewrites at least four of them as specific bullet points that name what they did and what came of it, entirely from their own genuine experience.
safetyNotes: No fabricated experience, title, or outcome is ever acceptable; every bullet point must describe something that genuinely happened.
materials: a list of real activities: school clubs, volunteering, informal work, projects, or extracurriculars

tasks.directions: List every real activity you have done that could reasonably appear on a first resume, even if it seems minor.

prompts.text: List at least six real activities, however small they seem, without judging yet whether they belong.

tasks.directions: Rewrite at least four activities as bullet points using an action verb plus a specific, honest result.

prompts.text: Write four bullet points, each starting with an action verb and naming a specific, true result or outcome.
Every bullet point describes something that genuinely happened, with nothing invented or exaggerated.

tasks.directions: Choose which activities are the strongest match for the kind of work you're interested in, and put those first.

prompts.text: Explain why you ordered your bullet points the way you did.

tasks.directions: Reflect on what surprised you about this process.

prompts.text: Which activity surprised you by turning into a stronger bullet point than you expected, and what specific detail made it stronger?

remediation: If a learner's bullet points are vague ('helped out at events') with no specific action or result, reteach by modeling the pattern 'action verb + what you actually did + what came of it' on one worked example, then have the learner rewrite two of their weakest bullet points using that pattern.
extension: Have the learner rewrite their four bullet points a second time targeted at a specific job title from Unit 1, choosing different details to emphasize depending on what that job actually values.
